core.big_idea: The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.

passages.reading_note: Read the central passage in context; select age-appropriate portions when needed.

core.metanarrative_position: Jesus' ministry: The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.

claims.statement: Luke says he investigated matters and wrote an orderly account.
Luke addresses a named reader, Theophilus, and states a purpose of certainty regarding what he had been taught.
John says Jesus did many other signs not written in his book.
John states that his selected signs were written so readers may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.
The four canonical Gospels can be read as complementary witnesses, but these two passages alone do not explain every difference among them.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not state this claim more strongly than its evidence classification allows.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify author/audience/genre; observe context; distinguish direct statement, inference, and application.

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from Luke 1:1-4; John 20:30-31 that the four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
learning.extension_objective: Identify context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from reasonable inference and application.
know: The central passage is Luke 1:1-4; John 20:30-31.
The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
The lesson belongs within the wider biblical storyline.
understand: Meaning depends on context and genre.
Application should follow what the text supports rather than replace it.
practise: State one observation before giving an interpretation.
Compare the opening or closing purpose statements of two Gospels and note one similarity and one difference.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the central passage.
Student can state the big idea without unsupported details.
Student can distinguish at least one observation from one application.

zero_prep_card.objective: Explain from Luke 1:1-4; John 20:30-31 that the four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do you notice first in this passage before we explain what it means?
say: Luke says he investigated matters and wrote an orderly account.
Luke addresses a named reader, Theophilus, and states a purpose of certainty regarding what he had been taught.
John says Jesus did many other signs not written in his book.
The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
ask: What happens or is said in the passage?
What does this show about Jesus, God, people, or the biblical story?
Which statement is directly in the text?
What is one careful response for us?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete the Gospel Purpose Observation Grid activity.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray using one truth from the passage and one faithful response.

preparation.passage_context: Jesus' ministry: The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
text_observations: Luke says he investigated matters and wrote an orderly account.
Luke addresses a named reader, Theophilus, and states a purpose of certainty regarding what he had been taught.
John says Jesus did many other signs not written in his book.
John states that his selected signs were written so readers may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to broader synthesis.
Keep genre, original audience, and immediate context visible.
Label synthesis, inference, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: Do not claim these verses by themselves prove every traditional claim about Gospel authorship.
Do not force every difference among Gospel accounts into an artificial harmonisation.
Distinguish what Luke and John explicitly say from later historical information.

likely_questions.question: Why are some stories different in different Gospels?
likely_questions.purpose: Different authors can select and arrange material for different purposes. Specific differences should be studied passage by passage rather than explained away in advance.

likely_questions.question: Does “different” mean “contradictory”?
likely_questions.purpose: Not automatically. A difference can be complementary, but each alleged contradiction should be examined on its own evidence.

activities.learning_link: Makes the lesson’s interpretation skill visible and concrete.

steps: Work through the resource using the passage.

activities.low_resource_alternative: Use verbal thumbs-up/down responses instead of cards.
steps: Students identify whether each is directly in the passage or a conclusion.
Ask what evidence would be needed for each conclusion.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for the truth in this passage and ask for wisdom to respond faithfully.
closing.take_home_line: The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.

family.title: Why Four Gospels?
family.parent_intro: Use the passage itself first. Keep the conversation concrete, honest, and free from pressure.

flow.instructions: Ask one simple question that links the theme to ordinary life.
Read selected portions of Luke 1:1-4; John 20:30-31. Ask what everyone notices.
Say the big idea in your own words: The four Gospels provide complementary, purposeful witnesses to Jesus.
Use the Gospel Purpose Observation Grid idea verbally or on paper.
Compare the opening or closing purpose statements of two Gospels and note one similarity and one difference.

questions: What does the passage directly say?
What does it show about God, Jesus, people, or the big story?
What is one response we can practise this week?

interactive.title: Gospel Purpose Observation Grid
interactive.instructions: Sort or classify the lesson statements using the passage as evidence.

family.weekly_action: Compare the opening or closing purpose statements of two Gospels and note one similarity and one difference.
family.prayer: Thank God for what the passage reveals and ask for help to respond faithfully.
family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, or a public religious decision. If a sensitive concern emerges, respond calmly and involve an appropriate trusted adult.

quiz.question: What is the principal passage for Why Four Gospels??
quiz.explanation: The lesson is governed by its principal passage.

quiz.question: Which comes first in careful Bible reading?
quiz.explanation: Observe what the text says before moving to interpretation or application.

quiz.question: Luke says he investigated matters and wrote an orderly account.
quiz.explanation: This statement is directly supported by the principal passage.

quiz.question: Should an interpretation be presented as a quotation from the text when the text does not directly say it?
quiz.explanation: Interpretation and inference should be labelled honestly.

puzzle.title: Evidence Order
puzzle.instructions: Put the reading process in a responsible order.

printables.title: Gospel Purpose Observation Grid
printables.purpose: Support the primary activity for Why Four Gospels?.

accessibility.reading_level: Age-appropriate Bible reading with scaffolded discussion
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms from the passage before using theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read the passage aloud and use icons, sequence cards, or oral choices.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the passage, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults rather than solving them in class.
